status: proposed alternatives for review. Nothing here is applied to the baseline or to any earlier package, and nothing is owner-approved.

concern.statement: The baseline epoch range is [1, 2^64-1]. The fmt-2 value {fmt, epoch, seq, tomb, b64} does not fix the JSON type of epoch. If epoch is a JSON number, every JS reader holds it as an IEEE-754 double, which is exact only up to 2^53. The 0.13 reference therefore rejects value epochs above 2^53-1 (epochNotJsSafe), which narrows the domain.

provedWith.effect: the value no longer equals the record name's epoch 0020000000000001: decode reports 'epoch', so the record is corrupt and the generation cannot recover
2^64 is outside [1, 2^64-1]: the largest legal epoch cannot be stored as a number at all
exact; the first collision is 2^53 + 1 with 2^53

concern.reading: JSON.parse maps an integer literal to the nearest double (round half to even); Python float() of the same literal computes the same nearest double, which the runner uses as the model. The root may confirm in Node with tools/js_number_probe.cjs.
concern.practicalReach: Reaching 2^53 needs 2^53 worker generations, so the concern is about the declared domain, not about expected use. Narrowing the domain is still a baseline change and is not done silently.

alternatives.name: hex16 string
alternatives.text: epoch is the same 16 lowercase hex digits as the record name, as a JSON string. The decoder requires ^[0-9a-f]{16}$, a value in [1, 2^64-1], equal to the name's epoch. seq stays a JSON number (<= 2^32-1, exact in JS).
alternatives.cost: +2 bytes for the largest JS-safe epoch (16 digits -> 18 characters with quotes). The maximum model record becomes enc = 1442009 <= RECORD_BYTES_MAX 1442048 (was 1442007); P-E4-4's netKey bound becomes <= 105 characters (was 107).
alternatives.baselineImpact: fills an unspecified type (browser.md:534 fixes field names only); RECORD_BYTES_MAX, names, ranges and limits are unchanged

alternatives.name: decimal string
alternatives.text: epoch as a canonical decimal string (no sign, no leading zero), 1..20 digits.
alternatives.cost: largest value 22 characters with quotes; enc 1442013 for the maximum record
alternatives.drawback: a second canonical form of the same number besides the name's hex

alternatives.name: BigInt-aware number
alternatives.text: keep a JSON number and read it with a BigInt-aware parser.
alternatives.drawback: the value is written through chrome.storage, whose values are JSON-serialisable data; a BigInt is not (JSON.stringify(1n) throws TypeError), and a Number cannot carry the value before it is written. Not feasible on the storage path.

alternatives.name: cap at 2^53-1
alternatives.drawback: narrows the baseline domain [1, 2^64-1]: a baseline change that needs the owner. Not recommended.

maxRecord.rule: the 0.13 maximum record (4096 entries 'K0000'..'K0fff' -> 251 x 'a'; netKey '0x'+64 x '1'; addr '0x'+40 x '2'; name length 142) with epoch 2^64-1 and seq 2^32-1

oldCodecPreserved.note: the 0.13 reference keeps rejecting; nothing older changes

recommendedAmendment: Proposal (not applied): in browser.md:534-535 add 'epoch is the record name's 16 lowercase hex digits as a JSON string; seq is a JSON integer'. Update annex E4 section 4 decoder rules and P-E4-4 (netKey <= 105). Decider: root reviewer, as a representation detail the baseline leaves open; if root classifies it as a baseline change, the owner.
